127573.subject: Botany
127573.text: What is secondary productivity in an ecosystem?
options: The rate of production of organic matter during photosynthesis
The rate of formation of new organic matter by consumers
127573.sol: A constant input of solar energy is the basic requirement for any ecosystem to function and sustain. Primary production is defined as the amount of biomass or organic matter produced per unit area over a time period by plants during photosynthesis. It is expressed in terms of weight (g m–2) or energy (kcal m–2). The rate of biomass production is called productivity. It is expressed in terms of gm–2 yr –1 or (kcal m–2) yr–1 to compare the productivity of different ecosystems. It can be divided into gross primary productivity (GPP) and net primary productivity (NPP). Gross primary productivity of an ecosystem is the rate of production of organic matter during photosynthesis. A considerable amount of GPP is utilised by plants in respiration. Gross primary productivity minus respiration losses (R), is the net primary productivity (NPP). GPP – R = NPP Net primary productivity is the available biomass for the consumption to heterotrophs (herbiviores and decomposers). Secondary productivity is defined as the rate of formation of new organic matter by consumers. Primary productivity depends on the plant species inhabiting a particular area. It also depends on a variety of environmental factors, availability of nutrients and photosynthetic capacity of plants. Therefore, it varies in different types of ecosystems. The annual net primary productivity of the whole biosphere is approximately 170 billion tons (dry weight) of organic matter. Of this, despite occupying about 70 per cent of the surface, the productivity of the oceans are only 55 billion tons. Rest of course, is on land. Discuss the main reason for the low productivity of ocean with your teacher.
127573.meta: What is secondary productivity in an ecosystem?

128824.subject: Zoology
128824.text: What is the purpose of blood coagulation?
128824.sol: Blood exhibits coagulation or clotting in response to an injury or trauma. This is a mechanism to prevent excessive loss of blood from the body. You would have observed a dark reddish brown scum formed at the site of a cut or an injury over a period of time. It is a clot or coagulam formed mainly of a network of threads called fibrins in which dead and damaged formed elements of blood are trapped. Fibrins are formed by the conversion of inactive fibrinogens in the plasma by the enzyme thrombin. Thrombins, in turn are formed from another inactive substance present in the plasma called prothrombin. An enzyme complex, thrombokinase, is required for the above reaction. This complex is formed by a series of linked enzymic reactions (cascadeprocess) involving a number of factors present in the plasma in an inactive state. An injury or a trauma stimulates the platelets in the blood to release certain factors which activate the mechanism of coagulation. Certain factors released by the tissues at the site of injury also can initiate coagulation. Calcium ions play a very important role in clotting.
128824.meta: What is the purpose of blood coagulation?

128913.subject: Zoology
128913.text: What does the T-wave represent in an ECG?
128913.sol: The P-wave represents the electrical excitation (or depolarisation) of the atria, which leads to the contraction of both the atria. The QRS complex represents the depolarisation of the ventricles, which initiates the ventricular contraction. The contraction starts shortly after Q and marks the beginning of the systole. The T-wave represents the return of the ventricles from excited to normal state (repolarisation). The end of the T-wave marks the end of systole. Obviously, by counting the number of QRS complexes that occur in a given time period, one can determine the heart beat rate of an individual. Since the ECGs obtained from different individuals have roughly the same shape for a given lead configuration, any deviation from this shape indicates a possible abnormality or disease. Hence, it is of a great clinical significance..

129470.subject: Zoology
129470.text: What type of excretory structures are found in most vertebrates?
129470.sol: A survey of animal kingdom presents a variety of excretory structures. In most of the invertebrates, these structures are simple tubular forms whereas vertebrates have complex tubular organs called kidneys. Some of these structures are mentioned here. Protonephridia or flame cells are the excretory structures in Platyhelminthes (Flatworms, e.g., Planaria), rotifers, some annelids and the cephalochordate – Amphioxus. Protonephridia are primarily concerned with ionic and fluid volume regulation, i.e., osmoregulation. Nephridia are the tubular excretory structures of earthworms and other annelids. Nephridia help to remove nitrogenous wastes and maintain a fluid and ionic balance. Malpighian tubules are the excretory structures of most of the insects including cockroaches. Malpighian tubules help in the removal of nitrogenous wastes and osmoregulation. Antennal glands or green glands perform the excretory function in crustaceans like prawns.

130581.subject: Zoology
130581.text: How long do females need to take oral contraceptive pills each cycle?
130581.sol: Oral administration of small doses of either progestogens or progestogen–estrogen combinations is another contraceptive method used by the females. They are used in the form of tablets and hence are popularly called the pills. Pills have to be taken daily for a period of 21 days starting preferably within the first five days of menstrual cycle. After a gap of 7 days (during which menstruation occurs) it has to be repeated in the same pattern till the female desires to prevent conception. They inhibit ovulation and implantation as well as alter the quality of cervical mucus to prevent/retard entry of sperms. Pills are very effective with lesser side effects and are well accepted by the females. Saheli–the new oral contraceptive for the females contains a non-steroidal preparation. It is a ‘once a week’ pill with very few side effects and high contraceptive value.

130793.subject: Zoology
130793.text: A married couple seeks medical help for infertility. Clinical evaluation reveals that the female partner has normal, patent fallopian tubes and a normal uterus, but her ovaries fail to produce viable ova. The male partner has a normal sperm count and normal sperm motility. Which of the following Assisted Reproductive Technologies (ART) is the most suitable for this couple?
130793.sol:
The female partner cannot produce ova but can provide a suitable environment for fertilization and further embryonic development, as her fallopian tubes and uterus are normal. The male partner has normal sperm parameters.

In such cases, the most suitable technique is GIFT (Gamete Intra Fallopian Transfer). An ovum collected from a donor is transferred into the fallopian tube of the female, allowing in-vivo fertilization by the male partner's sperms.

ZIFT and ICSI involve in-vitro fertilization, which is unnecessary here since natural in-vivo fertilization is possible. IUI (Intra Uterine Insemination) is used when the male partner has a low sperm count or inability to inseminate, which is not the case here.

Answer: GIFT

130859.subject: Zoology
130859.text: What is the function of the oviducts in the female reproductive system?
options: Transport of ovum from ovary to uterus
130859.sol: The oviducts (fallopian tubes), uterus and vagina constitute the female accessory ducts. Each fallopian tube is about 10-12 cm long and extends from the periphery of each ovary to the uterus, the part closer to the ovary is the funnel-shaped infundibulum. The edges of the infundibulum possess finger-like projections called fimbriae, which help in collection of the ovum after ovulation. The infundibulum leads to a wider part of the oviduct called ampulla. The last part of the oviduct, isthmus has a narrow lumen and it joins the uterus

130886.text: What does the head of a sperm contain?

The head of a sperm contains enzymes that help fertilization
130886.sol: It is a microscopic structure composed of a head, neck, a middle piece and a tail. A plasma membrane envelops the whole body of sperm. The sperm head contains an elongated haploid nucleus, the anterior portion of which is covered by a cap-like structure, acrosome. The acrosome is filled with enzymes that help fertilisation of the ovum. The middle piece possesses numerous mitochondria, which produce energy for the movement of tail that facilitate sperm motility essential for fertilisation. The human male ejaculates about 200 to 300 million sperms during a coitus of which, for normal fertility, at least 60 per cent sperms must have normal shape and size and at least 40 per cent of them must show vigorous motility

131439.subject: Zoology
131439.text: What are the regions of chromatin referred to as that are more densely packed and stains dark?
131439.sol: The beads-on-string structure in chromatin is packaged to form chromatin fibers that are further coiled and condensed at the metaphase stage of cell division to form chromosomes. The packaging of chromatin at higher levels requires an additional set of proteins that collectively are referred to as Non-histone Chromosomal (NHC) proteins. In a typical nucleus, some regions of chromatin are loosely packed (and stains light) and are referred to as euchromatin. The chromatin that is more densely packed and stains dark are called Heterochromatin. Euchromatin is said to be transcriptionally active chromatin, whereas heterochromatin is inactive.

132259.subject: Zoology
132259.text: Under what condition would a daughter be color blind according to the paragraph?
options: If her mother is color blind and her father is a carrier
If her mother is a carrier and her father is color blind
If both her parents are carriers
If her mother is color blind and her father is normal
132259.sol: It is a sex-linked recessive disorder due to defect in either red or green cone of eye resulting in failure to discriminate between red and green colour. This defect is due to mutation in certain genes present in the X chromosome. It occurs in about 8 per cent of males and only about 0.4 per cent of females. This is because the genes that lead to red-green colour blindness are on the X chromosome. Males have only one X chromosome and females have two. The son of a woman who carries the gene has a 50 per cent chance of being colour blind. The mother is not herself colour blind because the gene is recessive. That means that its effect is suppressed by her matching dominant normal gene. A daughter will not normally be colour blind, unless her mother is a carrier and her father is colour blind.

132429.subject: Zoology
132429.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Thalassemia differs from sickle-cell anaemia as the former is a quantitative problem of synthesising too few globin molecules.
Reason (R): Sickle-cell anaemia is a qualitative problem of synthesising an incorrectly functioning globin.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true.
132429.sol:
Thalassemia and sickle-cell anaemia are both autosomal recessive blood disorders.

According to NCERT, Thalassemia differs from sickle-cell anaemia in that the former is a quantitative problem of synthesising too few globin molecules, while the latter is a qualitative problem of synthesising an incorrectly functioning globin.

Therefore, both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true independent statements. However, Reason (R) describes the nature of sickle-cell anaemia and does not explain why Thalassemia is a quantitative problem (which is due to mutation or deletion of genes controlling globin chain synthesis).

Hence, both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

Answer: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

They provide insight into past life-forms and evolutionary changes

Hence, new forms of life have arisen at different times in the history of earth. All this is called paleontological evidence. Studying extinct organisms like dinosaurs through fossils helps understand past life-forms and evolutionary changes over time.Fossils are described as the remains of the hard parts of life-forms found in rocks.Rocks form sediments and a cross-section of earth's crust indicates the arrangement of sediments one over the other during the long history of earth. 133554.text:
Match List-I with List-II regarding drug-yielding plants and their physiological effects.

List-I (Plant)List-II (Effect/Property)
(A) Papaver somniferum(I) Affects cardiovascular system of the body
(B) Erythroxylum coca(II) Possesses hallucinogenic properties
(C) Cannabis sativa(III) Depressant that slows down body functions
(D) Datura(IV) Interferes with the transport of dopamine

133554.sol:
Papaver somniferum yields opioids (such as heroin), which bind to specific opioid receptors in the central nervous system and gastrointestinal tract, acting as a depressant that slows down body functions.

Erythroxylum coca yields cocaine, which interferes with the transport of the neurotransmitter dopamine.

Cannabis sativa yields cannabinoids, which are known for their effects on the cardiovascular system of the body.

Datura contains alkaloids that possess hallucinogenic properties.

Therefore, the correct match is (A)-(III), (B)-(IV), (C)-(I), (D)-(II).

Answer: (A)-(III), (B)-(IV), (C)-(I), (D)-(II)

134470.text: What is the ability of plasmids and bacteriophages in bacterial cells?
options: Replicating within control of chromosomal DNA
Replicating independently of the control of chromosomal DNA
Replicating with control of chromosomal DNA
134470.sol: You know that plasmids and bacteriophages have the ability to replicate within bacterial cells independent of the control of chromosomal DNA. Bacteriophages because of their high number per cell, have very high copy numbers of their genome within the bacterial cells. Some plasmids may have only one or two copies per cell whereas others may have >15-100 copies per cell. Their numbers can go even higher. If we are able to link an alien piece of DNA with bacteriophage or plasmid DNA, we can multiply its numbers equal to the copy number of the plasmid or bacteriophage. Vectors used at present, are engineered in such a way that they help easy linking of foreign DNA and selection of recombinants from non-recombinants

134497.subject: Zoology
134497.text: What type of virus has the ability to transform normal cells into cancerous cells?
134497.sol: Similarly, retroviruses in animals have the ability to transform normal cells into cancerous cells. A better understanding of the art of delivering genes by pathogens in their eukaryotic hosts has generated knowledge to transform these tools of pathogens into useful vectors for delivering genes of interest to humans. The tumor inducing (Ti) plasmid of Agrobacterium tumifaciens has now been modified into a cloning vector which is no more pathogenic to the plants but is still able to use the mechanisms to deliver genes of our interest into a variety of plants. Similarly, retroviruses have also been disarmed and are now used to deliver desirable genes into animal cells. So, once a gene or a DNA fragment has been ligated into a suitable vector it is transferred into a bacterial, plant or animal host (where it multiplies).

134791.subject: Zoology
134791.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): In recombinant DNA technology, DNA ligase is required to create hydrogen bonds between the complementary sticky ends of the vector and foreign DNA.
Reason (R): Restriction endonucleases inspect the length of a DNA sequence to find their specific recognition sequence and cut the sugar-phosphate backbone.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion.
Assertion is false but Reason is true.
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion.
Assertion is true but Reason is false.
134791.sol:
The Assertion is false. In recombinant DNA technology, the sticky ends of the vector and foreign DNA naturally form hydrogen bonds with their complementary cut counterparts. DNA ligase is not required for hydrogen bonding; rather, it is required to form covalent phosphodiester bonds to seal the sugar-phosphate backbones of the joined DNA fragments.

The Reason is true. According to NCERT, each restriction endonuclease functions by inspecting the length of a DNA sequence. Once it finds its specific recognition sequence, it binds to the DNA and cuts each of the two strands of the double helix at specific points in their sugar-phosphate backbones.

Therefore, Assertion is false but Reason is true.

Answer: Assertion is false but Reason is true.

134859.subject: Zoology
134859.text: A genetic engineer is attempting to introduce a human gene into the plasmid vector pBR322. If the human DNA fragment was isolated by digesting the human genome with the restriction enzyme BamH I, which of the following enzymes must be used to cleave the pBR322 plasmid to ensure successful ligation?
134859.sol:
For a recombinant DNA molecule to be created, both the source DNA (human gene) and the vector DNA (pBR322) must be cut with the same restriction endonuclease.

Using the same restriction enzyme ensures that both DNA molecules have complementary sticky ends, which can then be joined by the enzyme DNA ligase.

Since the human DNA was cut with BamH I, the pBR322 plasmid must also be cut with BamH I. Using any other enzyme (like EcoR I, Sal I, or Hind III) would generate incompatible ends that cannot be ligated.

Answer: BamH I

301914.text: If $\sin A+\sin B+\sin C=0$ and $\cos A+\cos B+\cos C=0$, then $\cos (A+B)+\cos (B+C)+\cos (C+A)$ is equal to
301914.sol:
Here, we have the pattern of data in $\cos x$ and $\sin x$, so let's use the method of polar form of complex number.
Polar form of complex number,
$z=\cos \theta+i \sin \theta$
then $\bar{z}=\cos \theta-i \sin \theta$
and $z \bar{z}=1\Rightarrow \quad \bar{z}=\frac{1}{z}$
Let $z_1=\cos A+i \sin Az_2=\cos B+i \sin B$
and $z_3=\cos C+i \sin C$
Then, $\quad \bar{z}_1=\cos A-i \sin A\begin{gathered}
\bar{z}_2=\cos B-i \sin B \\
z_3=\cos C-\sin C
\end{gathered}$
Now, to find $\cos (A+B)+\cos (B+C)+\cos (C+A)\begin{aligned}
& \bar{z}_1+\bar{z}_2+\bar{z}_3=(\cos A-i \sin A) \\
& +(\cos B-i \sin B)+(\cos C-i \sin C) \\
& =(\cos A+\cos B+\cos C)-i(\sin A+\sin B+\sin C)=0 \\
& \frac{1}{z_1}+\frac{1}{z_2}+\frac{1}{z_3}=0 \quad\left[\because \quad \bar{z}=\frac{1}{z}\right] \\
& z_1 z_2+z_2 z_3+z_3 z_1=0 \\
& \sum(\cos A+i \sin A)(\cos B+i \sin B)=0 \\
& \sum(\cos A \cos B-\sin A \sin B) \\
& +i(\sin A \cos B+\cos A \sin B)=0 \\
& \sum \cos (A+B)+i \sin (A+B)=0 \\
& \sum \cos (A+B)=0
\end{aligned}$
Comparing the real part, we get
$\cos (A+B)+\cos (B+C)+\cos (C+A)=0$

Initially, the gas is at $300K$ and occupies a volume of $2 .4 \times {10}^{- 3}m^{3}$ and the spring is in its relaxed position. Now, gas is slowly heated by a small electric heater and the piston moves out slowly by $0 .1 m$. Calculate the final temperature of the gas and the heat supplied by the heater. 303477.text: A ball is projected vertically upward at a speed of $50 \text{ m/s}$. Determine the speed at half the maximum height. Take $g = 10 \text{ m/s}^2$.
303477.sol:
Initial speed $u = 50 \text{ m/s}$

Maximum height $H = \dfrac{u^2}{2g}$

Let $v$ be the speed at half the maximum height, $h = \dfrac{H}{2}$.

Using the equation of motion:

$v^2 = u^2 - 2gh$

$v^2 = u^2 - 2g \left(\dfrac{H}{2}\right)

$v^2 = u² - gH$

Substituting $H = $\dfrac{u^2}{2g}:

$v^2 = u² - g \left(\dfrac{u^2}{2g}\right) =$u^2 - $\dfrac{u^2}{2} = \dfrac{u^2}{2}

$v = $\dfrac{u}{\sqrt{2}}

$v = $\dfrac{50}{\sqrt{2}} ==25\sqrt{2} \text{ m/s}

303487.text: From a point $100 \text{ m}$ above the ground, a ball is thrown horizontally with a speed of $20 \text{ m/s}$. Determine the horizontal distance the ball travels before reaching the ground in meters.
303487.sol:
Let the time taken by the ball to reach the ground be $t$.

Using the second equation of motion in the vertical direction:

$h = u_y t + \dfrac{1}{2} g t^2$

Since the ball is thrown horizontally, the initial vertical velocity $u_y = 0$. Assuming $g = 10 \text{ m/s}^2$:

$100 = 0 + \dfrac{1}{2} (10) t^2$

$100 = 5t^2$

$t^2 = 20 \Rightarrow t = \sqrt{20} = 2\sqrt{5} \text{ s}$

The horizontal distance (range) traveled by the ball is given by:

$R = u_x \times t$

$R = 20 \times 2\sqrt{5} = 40\sqrt{5} \text{ m}$

303989.subject: Physics
303989.text: Assume all surfaces depicted in the diagram lack friction. The car has a mass $M$, the block has a mass $m$, and the spring possesses a force constant $k$. The system is released from rest with the spring initially stretched by a distance $x_0$. Determine the time period of the resulting simple harmonic motions.
303989.sol:
Let $x_1$ and $x_2$ be the displacements of the block of mass $m$ and the car of mass $M$ from their respective equilibrium positions.

Since no external horizontal force acts on the system, the center of mass remains stationary. Therefore:

$m x_1 + M x_2 = 0 \Rightarrow x_2 = -\dfrac{m}{M} x_1$

The net extension or compression in the spring is the relative displacement $x = x_1 - x_2$.

Substituting the value of $x_2$, we get:

$x = x_1 - \left(-\dfrac{m}{M} x_1\right) = x_1 \left(1 + \dfrac{m}{M}\right) = x_1 \left(\dfrac{M + m}{M}\right)$

The restoring force acting on the block of mass $m$ is $F = -kx$.

$F = -k \left(\dfrac{M + m}{M}\right) x_1$

The acceleration of the block is $a_1 = \dfrac{F}{m} = -\dfrac{k(M + m)}{mM} x_1$.

Comparing this with the standard equation of simple harmonic motion $a = -\omega^2 x$, we find the angular frequency $\omega$:

$\omega^2 = \dfrac{k(M + m)}{mM} \Rightarrow \omega = \sqrt{\dfrac{k(M + m)}{mM}}$

The time period of oscillation is given by $T = \dfrac{2\pi}{\omega}$:

$T = 2\pi \sqrt{\dfrac{mM}{k(M + m)}}$

Alternatively, this is a standard two-body oscillator problem where the time period is given by $T = 2\pi \sqrt{\dfrac{\mu}{k}}$, with the reduced mass $\mu = \dfrac{mM}{M + m}$.

304339.text: A slide in a park possesses a total length of $10 ext{ m}$ and a height of $8.0 ext{ m}$. A vertical ladder is provided to reach the top. A boy weighing $200 ext{ N}$ ascends the ladder to the upper end of the slide, then slides down to the ground. The slide offers an average friction equal to three tenths of his weight. Calculate the work done by the slide on the boy as he comes down. Neglect any work done by forces inside the body of the boy.
304339.sol:
Given:
Length of the slide, $s = 10 \text{ m}$
Weight of the boy, $W = 200 \text{ N}$
Average friction force, $f = \dfrac{3}{10}W = \dfrac{3}{10} \times 200 = 60 \text{ N}$

The slide exerts two forces on the boy: normal reaction and frictional force.

The work done by the normal reaction is zero because it is perpendicular to the direction of motion.

The work done by the frictional force is:
$W_f = -f \times s$
$W_f = -60 \times 10 = -600 \text{ J}$

Total work done by the slide on the boy is:
$W_{\text{slide}} = W_N + W_f = 0 - 600 = -600 \text{ J}$

304801.text: A vertical tube with a semicircular cross section contains a liquid, as shown in the figure. The contact angle is zero. The ratio of the surface tension force acting on the curved part to the surface tension force on the flat part is
304801.sol:
Let the radius of the semicircular cross-section of the tube be $R$.

The surface tension force acting on any part of the wall is given by $F = T \times l \times \cos\theta$, where $T$ is the surface tension of the liquid, $l$ is the length of the line of contact, and $\theta$ is the contact angle.

Given that the contact angle $\theta = 0^{{}^{{}^{\circ}}}$, we have $\cos\theta = 1$. Thus, the force is simply proportional to the length of contact, $F = T \times l$.

For the curved part, the length of the line of contact is the arc length of the semicircle:
$l_c = \pi R$
Therefore, the surface tension force on the curved part is:
$F_c = T \times \pi R$

For the flat part, the length of the line of contact is the diameter of the semicircle:
$l_f = 2R$
Therefore, the surface tension force on the flat part is:
$F_f = T \times 2R$

The ratio of the surface tension force acting on the curved part to that on the flat part is:
$\dfrac{F_c}{F_f} = \dfrac{T \times \pi R}{T \times 2R} = \dfrac{\pi}{2}$

305252.subject: Physics
305252.text: Consider an infinite ladder constructed using $1\ \Omega$ and $2\ \Omega$ resistors, as shown in the figure. Determine the effective resistance between points $A$ and $B$.
305252.sol:
Let the effective resistance of the infinite ladder between points A and B be $R$.

Since the ladder is infinite, removing the first repeating unit (one $1\ \Omega$ resistor in series and one $2\ \Omega$ resistor in parallel) leaves an identical infinite ladder across the next nodes. Therefore, the resistance of the remaining infinite ladder is also $R$.

The equivalent circuit can be simplified to a $1\ \Omega$ resistor in series with the parallel combination of a $2\ \Omega$ resistor and $R$.

The equation for the equivalent resistance is:
$R = 1 + \dfrac{2R}{2 + R}$

Solving for $R$:
$R = \dfrac{2 + R + 2R}{2 + R}$

$R = \dfrac{3R + 2}{R + 2}$

$R(R + 2) = 3R + 2$

$R^2 + 2R = 3R + 2$

$R^2 - R - 2 = 0$

Factorizing the quadratic equation:
$(R - 2)(R + 1) = 0$

Since resistance cannot be negative, we discard $R = -1\ \Omega$.

Thus, $R = 2\ \Omega$.

305417.subject: Physics
305417.text: A circular ring of radius $r$ is uniformly charged with a linear charge density $\lambda$. Determine the electric potential at a point on the axis located at a distance $x$ from the centre of the ring. Subsequently, use this potential expression to determine the electric field at the same point.
305417.sol:
Consider an elemental charge $dq$ on the ring of radius $r$. The linear charge density is $\lambda$, so $dq = \lambda dl$.

The total charge on the ring is $Q = \int \lambda dl = \lambda (2\pi r)$.

The electric potential $V$ at a point on the axis at a distance $x$ from the centre is given by integrating the potential due to each elemental charge:

$V = \int \dfrac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0} \dfrac{dq}{\sqrt{r^2 + x^2}}$

Since the distance $\sqrt{r^2 + x^2}$ is constant for all points on the ring:

$V = \dfrac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0 \sqrt{r^2 + x^2}} \int dq = \dfrac{Q}{4\pi\varepsilon_0 \sqrt{r^2 + x^2}}$

Substituting $Q = 2\pi r \lambda$:

$V = \dfrac{2\pi r \lambda}{4\pi\varepsilon_0 \sqrt{r^2 + x^2}} = \dfrac{r\lambda}{2\varepsilon_0 (r^2 + x^2)^{1/2}}$

The electric field $E$ along the axis is the negative gradient of the potential:

$E = -\dfrac{dV}{dx} = -\dfrac{d}{dx} \left( $\dfrac{r\lambda}{2\varepsilon_0} ($r^2 + x²)^{-1/2} \right)$

$E = $-\dfrac{r\lambda}{2\varepsilon_0} \left( $-\dfrac{1}{2} ($r^2 + x^2)^{-3/2} \times 2x \right)$

$E = $\dfrac{r\lambda x}{2\varepsilon_0 (r^2 + x^2)^{3/2}}$

306043.text: At a location where the angle of dip is $60^{}^{{}^{\circ}}$, the earth's magnetic field has a horizontal component of $26 \mu\text{T}$. Determine the vertical component as well as the magnitude of the magnetic field.
306043.sol:
Given angle of dip, $\delta = 60^{}^{{}^{\circ}}$

Horizontal component of earth's magnetic field, $B_H = 26 \mu\text{T}$

The vertical component $B_V$ is given by:

$B_V = B_H \tan\delta$

$B_V = 26 \tan 60^{}^{{}^{\circ}} = 26 \sqrt{3} \approx 26 \times 1.732 = 45.03 \mu\text{T} \approx 45 \mu\text{T}$

The magnitude of the earth's magnetic field $B$ is given by:

$B = \dfrac{B_H}{\cos\delta}$

$B = \dfrac{26}{\cos 60^{}^{{}^{\circ}}} = \dfrac{26}{1/2} = 52 \mu\text{T}$

Thus, the vertical component is $45 \mu\text{T}$ and the magnitude of the magnetic field is $52 \mu\text{T}$.

306345.text: Determine the charge required to pass through an electrolyte in order to liberate one atom of a monovalent material.
306345.sol:
For a monovalent material, the valency is $1$, which means one electron is involved in the liberation of one atom at the electrode.

The charge required to liberate one atom is equal to the magnitude of the charge of one electron.

$q = e = 1.6 \times 10^{-19} \text{ C}$

Alternatively, using Faraday's laws of electrolysis, the charge required to liberate one mole ($N_A$ atoms) of a monovalent substance is $1 \text{ F} \approx 96500 \text{ C}$.

The charge required for one atom is:

$q = \dfrac{F}{N_A} = \dfrac{96500}{6.022 \times 10^{23}} \approx 1.6 \times 10^{-19} \text{ C}$

306490.subject: Physics
306490.text: Which of the following pairs of scales can yield identical numerical values for the temperature of a body?
306490.sol:
The relation between the Fahrenheit and Kelvin scales is given by:

$\dfrac{F - 32}{180} = \dfrac{K - 273.15}{100}$

For the two scales to show the same reading, let $F = K = x$. Substituting this into the equation:

$\dfrac{x - 32}{9} = \dfrac{x - 273.15}{5}$

$5x - 160 = 9x - 2458.35$

$4x = 2298.35$

$x = 574.59$

Thus, the Fahrenheit and Kelvin scales can yield identical numerical values at $574.59$.

For Celsius and Kelvin, the relation is $K = C + 273.15$, which means they can never be equal.

For Fahrenheit and Rankine, the relation is $R = F + 459.67$, which means they can never be equal.

The platinum scale measures temperature in degrees Celsius, so it also cannot equal the Kelvin scale.

306567.subject: Physics
306567.text: As illustrated in the figure, two short magnets with equal dipole moments $M$ are joined perpendicularly at their centres. What is the magnitude of the magnetic field at a distance $d$ from the centre along the bisector of the right angle?
306567.sol:
Let the centre of the two magnets be at the origin $(0,0)$.

The horizontal magnet has its South pole on the left and North pole on the right. Its magnetic dipole moment is directed from South to North, so $\vec{M}_1 = M \hat{i}$.

The vertical magnet has its South pole at the bottom and North pole at the top. Its magnetic dipole moment is also directed from South to North, so $\vec{M}_2 = M \hat{j}$.

The net magnetic dipole moment of the system is the vector sum of the individual dipole moments:
$\vec{M}_{net} = \vec{M}_1 + \vec{M}_2 = M \hat{i} + M \hat{j}$

The magnitude of the net dipole moment is:
$|\vec{M}_{net}| = \sqrt{M^2 + M^2} = \sqrt{2}M$

The direction of $\vec{M}_{net}$ is at an angle of $45^{\circ}$ to the positive x-axis, which is along the bisector of the angle between the two North poles.

The point $P$ is at a distance $d$ along the bisector of the angle between the two South poles. This direction is exactly opposite to the direction of the net dipole moment. Therefore, the point $P$ lies on the axial line of the equivalent net dipole.

The magnitude of the magnetic field on the axial line of a short dipole at a distance $d$ is given by:
$B = \dfrac{\mu_0}{4\pi} \dfrac{2|\vec{M}_{net}|}{d^3}$

Substituting $|\vec{M}_{net}| = \sqrt{2}M$, we get:
$B = \dfrac{\mu_0}{4\pi} \dfrac{2\sqrt{2}M}{d^3}$

306824.text: Which among the following are electromagnetic waves?
306824.sol:
Gamma rays are high-frequency electromagnetic waves emitted from the nucleus of radioactive atoms.

Beta-minus rays are streams of electrons, beta-plus rays are streams of positrons, and $\alpha$-rays are streams of helium nuclei. These are all particulate radiations, not electromagnetic waves.

309252.subject: Chemistry
309252.text:
Identify the correct decreasing order of nucleophilicity for the following amines:

(i)

(ii)

(iii)
309252.sol:
Nucleophilicity of amines depends on the availability of the lone pair on the nitrogen atom for attack on an electrophile. Steric hindrance plays a major role in determining nucleophilicity; greater steric crowding around the nitrogen atom significantly decreases its nucleophilicity.

In compound (i) (quinuclidine), the alkyl groups are constrained in a rigid bicyclic ring system. This structural feature "ties back" the alkyl chains, exposing the lone pair on the nitrogen atom. Due to minimal steric hindrance, it is a highly effective nucleophile.

In compound (ii) (triethylamine), the three ethyl groups are flexible and can rotate, creating moderate steric hindrance around the nitrogen atom, making it less nucleophilic than compound (i).

In compound (iii) (triisopropylamine), the three isopropyl groups are highly bulky and cause severe steric crowding around the nitrogen atom. This effectively shields the lone pair, making it very difficult for the nitrogen to act as a nucleophile.

Therefore, the decreasing order of nucleophilicity is (i) > (ii) > (iii).

Answer: (i) > (ii) > (iii)

309432.subject: Chemistry
309432.text:
Arrange the following carboxylic acids in decreasing order of their acidic character:

(i)
(ii)
(iii)
(iv)
(v)
309432.sol:
The acidic strength of carboxylic acids depends on the stability of their conjugate base (carboxylate anion).

1. (v) 2,6-Dihydroxybenzoic acid: The conjugate base is highly stabilized by intramolecular hydrogen bonding from two ortho hydroxyl (-OH) groups. Additionally, the strong steric hindrance (ortho effect) forces the carboxylate group out of the plane of the benzene ring, preventing destabilizing resonance from the ring. This makes it the most acidic.

2. (ii) o-Hydroxybenzoic acid (Salicylic acid): The conjugate base is stabilized by intramolecular hydrogen bonding from one ortho -OH group, along with the ortho effect. It is highly acidic, but less so than (v).

3. (iv) o-Methoxybenzoic acid: The ortho -OCH_3$ group exerts an ortho effect (steric inhibition of resonance), which forces the -COOH group out of the plane, reducing the electron-donating resonance from the ring. Combined with the -I effect of the oxygen atom, it is more acidic than benzoic acid. However, it lacks the intramolecular hydrogen bonding seen in (ii) and (v).

4. (i) Benzoic acid: This serves as the reference compound.

5. (iii) p-Hydroxybenzoic acid: The -OH group is at the para position, where its strong +R (resonance) effect dominates over its -I effect. This increases the electron density on the carboxylate group, destabilizing the conjugate base and making it less acidic than benzoic acid.

Therefore, the decreasing order of acidic character is (v) > (ii) > (iv) > (i) > (iii).

Answer: (v) > (ii) > (iv) > (i) > (iii)$

310402.text: The moment of inertia of a rigid body in terms of its angular momentum $L$ and kinetic energy $K$ is
310402.sol:
Angular momentum of a rigid body about a fixed axis is given by

$L = I\omega$

Where $I$ is moment of inertia and $\omega$ is angular velocity about that axis.

Kinetic energy of body is given by

$K = \dfrac{1}{2}I{\omega}^{2}$

$∴K = \dfrac{1}{2I}{\left(I\omega\right)}^{2} = \dfrac{L^{2}}{2I}$

$⇒I = \dfrac{L^{2}}{2K}$

Consider a hydrogen like atom whose energy in $n^{\text {th }}$ excited state is given by

311995.sol:
Max" energy is liberated for transition
$E_n \rightarrow E_1$
and minimum energy for $E_n \rightarrow E_{n-1}$
Hence,
$\frac{E_1}{n^2}-\frac{E_1}{12}=52.224 \mathrm{eV}$
and $\quad \frac{E_1}{n^2}-\frac{E_1}{(n-1)^2}=1.224 \mathrm{eV}$
Solving we get,
$E_1=-54.4 \mathrm{eV}$
and $\quad n=5$
hence,
$E_1=-\frac{13.6 Z^2}{12}=-54.4$
$Z=2$

313515.text: In the coordinate plane, a point is called a lattice point if both of its coordinates are integers. Let $A$ be the point $(12,84)$. Find the number of right angled triangles $A B C$ in the coordinate plane where $B$ and $C$ are lattice points, having a right angle at the vertex $A$ and whose incenter is at the origin $(0,0)$.
313515.sol:
We know that if inradius is integer then sides of triangle is also integer.
Here $O A=60 \sqrt{2}$. Inradius $=60$ Hence $A B, B C, C A$ are integer. Let $A B=m^2-n^2$ $B C=m^2+n^2$ and $A C=2 m^2+n^2$ Here, $r=\frac{\Delta}{s}=\frac{m n \cdot\left(m^2-n^2\right)}{3(m+n)}=n(m-n)=60$ $\therefore n(m-n)=2^2 .3 .5 .$ $\therefore$ Possible values of $n$ are 12 . Then 12 such triangles are possible but when $B$ and $C$ interchange their position 12 more triangles are possible. Then total number of distinct triangles $=24$.

6a252ff498efbb6c17e92a1b.subject: Biology
6a252ff498efbb6c17e92a1b.text: Two species of herbivorous mammals inhabit the same savanna and rely on similar vegetation for food. To avoid competitive exclusion and successfully coexist in the same habitat, these species are most likely to:
options: synchronize their grazing schedules to feed simultaneously.
partition their resources by grazing on different parts of the plants.
increase their reproductive rate to aggressively outnumber the other species.
develop a predator-prey relationship with each other.
6a252ff498efbb6c17e92a1b.sol:
According to Gause's competitive exclusion principle, two species competing for the exact same resources cannot stably coexist. To avoid competitive exclusion and coexist in the same habitat, competing species often evolve to utilize different aspects of the shared resource, a process known as resource partitioning.

By grazing on different parts of the plants (for example, one species eating the tall stems while the other eats the lower leaves), the two herbivorous mammal species reduce direct competition, allowing both to survive in the same savanna.

Answer: partition their resources by grazing on different parts of the plants.

6a2a77befad2360f42564bbd.subject: Chemistry
6a2a77befad2360f42564bbd.text: In a particular thermodynamic process, a gas releases $250$ J of heat to its surroundings while $600$ J of work is done on it. What is the change in internal energy of the gas?
6a2a77befad2360f42564bbd.sol:
According to the first law of thermodynamics:

$\Delta Q = \Delta U + \Delta W$

Since heat is released by the gas to the surroundings, $\Delta Q = -250$ J.

Since work is done on the gas, $\Delta W = -600$ J.

Substituting these values into the first law equation:

$-250 = \Delta U - 600$

$\Delta U = 600 - 250 = +350$ J

Answer: $+350$ J

6a0e2779165ae1327797b3e3.subject: Biology
6a0e2779165ae1327797b3e3.text: Read the following statements regarding the Golgi apparatus and select the incorrect one.
options: The cis and trans faces of the organelle are entirely different but interconnected.
It is an important site for the formation of glycoproteins and glycolipids.
Vesicles from the endoplasmic reticulum fuse with the trans face and move towards the cis face.
The cis face is convex in shape and is also known as the forming face.
6a0e2779165ae1327797b3e3.sol:
The Golgi apparatus consists of a cis face (forming face) and a trans face (maturing face).

The cis face is convex in shape, while the trans face is concave.

Materials to be packaged in the form of vesicles from the endoplasmic reticulum fuse with the cis face of the Golgi apparatus and move towards the trans face.

Therefore, the statement that vesicles fuse with the trans face and move towards the cis face is incorrect.

The Golgi apparatus is an important site for the formation of glycoproteins and glycolipids.

The cis and trans faces are entirely different but interconnected.

Answer: Vesicles from the endoplasmic reticulum fuse with the trans face and move towards the cis face.

6a13e465688ac6d0667aad04.subject: Physics
6a13e465688ac6d0667aad04.text: An electric dipole consisting of two opposite charges of magnitude $4 \ \mu\text{C}$ separated by a distance of $5 \ \text{cm}$ is placed in a uniform electric field. If the maximum torque experienced by the dipole is $0.2 \ \text{N m}$, which of the following correctly gives the magnitude of the electric field ($E$) and the torque ($\tau$) when the dipole is oriented at $30^\circ$ to the field?
6a13e465688ac6d0667aad04.sol:
The dipole moment is given by $p = qd$.

Substituting the given values:

$p = (4 \times 10^{-6} \ \text{C}) \times (5 \times 10^{-2} \ \text{m}) = 2 \times 10^{-7} \ \text{C m}$

The maximum torque experienced by the dipole is $\tau_{\text{max}} = pE$.

$0.2 = (2 \times 10^{-7}) \times E$

$E = \dfrac{0.2}{2 \times 10^{-7}} = 10^6 \ \text{N C}^{-1}$

The torque at an angle $\theta = 30^\circ$ is given by $\tau = pE \sin \theta$.

$\tau = \tau_{\text{max}} \sin 30^\circ = 0.2 \times \dfrac{1}{2} = 0.1 \ \text{N m}$

Answer: $E = 10^6 \ \text{N C}^{-1}$ and $\tau = 0.1 \ \text{N m}$

Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Nucleotides are joined together by phosphodiester linkage between $5'$ and $3'$ carbon atoms of the pentose sugar.
Statement II: In the secondary structure of DNA, adenine forms three hydrogen bonds with thymine whereas cytosine forms two hydrogen bonds with guanine.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.
6a13e467688ac6d0667aad42.sol:
Statement I is correct because in a polynucleotide chain, nucleotides are linked together by phosphodiester linkages between the $3'$ carbon atom of the pentose sugar of one nucleotide and the $5'$ carbon atom of the pentose sugar of the adjacent nucleotide.

Statement II is incorrect because in the secondary structure of DNA, adenine pairs with thymine through two hydrogen bonds, whereas cytosine pairs with guanine through three hydrogen bonds.

Answer: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

6a16f3297cfacf7984f86753.subject: Biology
6a16f3297cfacf7984f86753.text:
Match List I with List II:

List IList II
ACommensalism1Cuscuta growing on hedge plants
BCompetition2Sea anemone and clownfish
CMutualism3Balanus dominating Chthamalus
DEctoparasitism4Fungi and roots of higher plants

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
6a16f3297cfacf7984f86753.sol:
Commensalism is an interaction where one species benefits and the other is neither harmed nor benefited. An example is the relationship between sea anemone and clownfish, where the clownfish gets protection from predators.

Competition occurs when two species compete for the same resources, often leading to the dominance of one over the other. The larger barnacle Balanus dominating the smaller Chthamalus is a classic example of competitive exclusion.

Mutualism is an interaction where both species benefit. Fungi and the roots of higher plants form mycorrhizae, where the fungi help in nutrient absorption and the plant provides carbohydrates.

Ectoparasitism involves a parasite living on the external surface of the host. Cuscuta is a parasitic vine that grows on hedge plants, deriving its nutrition from them.

Thus, the correct matching is A-2, B-3, C-4, D-1.

Answer: A-2, B-3, C-4, D-1

6a7a1ff8177f8ffa94232be1.subject: Physics
6a7a1ff8177f8ffa94232be1.text: Two projectiles are fired from the ground with the same initial speed, and they cover the same horizontal range. The ratio of their minimum speeds during flight is $1 : 3$. If the sum of their times of flight is $8$ s, the maximum height reached by the projectile that has the longer time of flight is (Take $g = 10$ m/s$^2$)
6a7a1ff8177f8ffa94232be1.sol:
For two projectiles to have the same horizontal range with the same initial speed $u$, their angles of projection must be $\theta$ and $90^\circ - \theta$.

The minimum speed of a projectile occurs at the highest point of its trajectory and is equal to the horizontal component of its velocity, $v_{\text{min}} = u \cos \theta$.

The ratio of their minimum speeds is given as $1 : 3$. Assuming $\theta$ is the steeper angle (so $\cos \theta$ is smaller):
$\dfrac{u \cos \theta}{u \cos (90^\circ - \theta)} = \dfrac{\cos \theta}{\sin \theta} = \cot \theta = \dfrac{1}{3}$
This implies $\tan \theta = 3$.

The times of flight are $t_1 = \dfrac{2u \sin \theta}{g}$ and $t_2 = \dfrac{2u \cos \theta}{g}$.
The ratio of their times of flight is:
$\dfrac{t_1}{t_2} = \dfrac{\sin \theta}{\cos \theta} = \tan \theta = 3$

We are given that the sum of their times of flight is $8$ s:
$t_1 + t_2 = 8$
Substituting $t_1 = 3t_2$ into the equation:
$3t_2 + t_2 = 8 \Rightarrow 4t_2 = 8 \Rightarrow t_2 = 2$ s
Thus, $t_1 = 6$ s.

The projectile with the longer time of flight has $t = 6$ s. The maximum height $H$ is related to the time of flight $t$ by:
$t = \dfrac{2u \sin \theta}{g} \Rightarrow u \sin \theta = \dfrac{gt}{2}$
$H = \dfrac{u^2 \sin^2 \theta}{2g} = \dfrac{\left(\dfrac{gt}{2}\right)^2}{2g} = \dfrac{g t^2}{8}$

Substituting $t = 6$ s and $g = 10$ m/s$^2$:
$H = \dfrac{10 \times (6)^2}{8} = \dfrac{10 \times 36}{8} = \dfrac{360}{8} = 45$ m

Answer: $45$ m

6a7a1ff877a427e6134780a8.text: A rigid cross is made of two identical uniform thin rods, each of mass $1.2 \text{ kg}$ and length $40 \text{ cm}$, joined at their centers at right angles. Four small point masses, each of mass $0.3 \text{ kg}$, are attached to the ends of the rods. The cross is mounted on a frictionless horizontal axle passing through its center. A light string is wrapped around a small cylindrical hub of radius $10 \text{ cm}$ fixed to the center of the cross, and a block of mass $2 \text{ kg}$ hangs from the free end of the string. If the system is released from rest, the angular acceleration of the cross is (Take $g = 10 \text{ m/s}^2$):
6a7a1ff877a427e6134780a8.sol:
Moment of inertia of the two rods about the central axis:
$I_{\text{rods}} = 2 \times \left(\dfrac{1}{12}M_{\text{r}}L^2\right) = 2 \times \dfrac{1}{12} \times 1.2 \times (0.4)^2 = 0.032 \text{ kg m}^2$.

Moment of inertia of the four point masses at distance $L/2$:
$I_{\text{masses}} = 4 \times m \left(\dfrac{L}{2}\right)^2 = 4 \times 0.3 \times (0.2)^2 = 0.048 \text{ kg m}^2$.

Total moment of inertia of the cross, $I = I_{\text{rods}} + I_{\text{masses}} = 0.032 + 0.048 = 0.08 \text{ kg m}^2$.

Let $T$ be the tension in the string and $a$ be the downward acceleration of the block.
Equation of motion for the block: $M_{\text{b}}g - T = M_{\text{b}}a$
Equation of motion for the cross: $TR_{\text{h}} = I\alpha$
Kinematic constraint: $a = \alpha R_{\text{h}}$

Substituting $a$ and $T$:
$M_{\text{b}}g - \dfrac{I\alpha}{R_{\text{h}}} = M_{\text{b}}(\alpha R_{\text{h}})$
$\alpha = \dfrac{M_{\text{b}}g}{M_{\text{b}}R_{\text{h}} + \dfrac{I}{R_{\text{h}}}} = \dfrac{M_{\text{b}}g R_{\text{h}}}{I + M_{\text{b}}R_{\text{h}}^2}$

Substituting the values:
$\alpha = \dfrac{2 \times 10 \times 0.1}{0.08 + 2 \times (0.1)^2} = \dfrac{2}{0.08 + 0.02} = \dfrac{2}{0.10} = 20 \text{ rad/s}^2$.

Answer: $20 \text{ rad/s}^2$

6a7a1ff8b127302f4a32d292.text: Two satellites $P$ and $Q$, having masses $m$ and $3m$ respectively, are revolving in circular orbits around a planet. If the orbital speeds of both the satellites are equal, which of the following physical quantities must also be identical for them?
6a7a1ff8b127302f4a32d292.sol:
The orbital speed of a satellite is given by $v = \sqrt{\dfrac{GM}{r}}$, where $M$ is the mass of the planet and $r$ is the orbital radius.

Since both satellites have the same orbital speed, their orbital radii $r$ must be equal.

The time period of revolution is $T = \dfrac{2\pi r}{v}$. Since both $r$ and $v$ are identical for the two satellites, their time periods must also be equal.

The other quantities depend on the mass of the satellite:
Kinetic energy $K = \dfrac{1}{2}mv^2$
Angular momentum $L = mvr$
Centripetal force $F = \dfrac{mv^2}{r}$

Because their masses are different, these dynamic quantities will not be identical.

Answer: Time period of revolution

6a7a1ff8db9defb2e78cc486.subject: Physics
6a7a1ff8db9defb2e78cc486.text: The root mean square (r.m.s) speed of the molecules of a rigid diatomic gas is $600\text{ m s}^{-1}$. If the molar mass of the gas is $30\text{ g mol}^{-1}$, the internal energy of one mole of this gas is
6a7a1ff8db9defb2e78cc486.sol:
The root mean square speed of a gas is given by:
$v_{\text{rms}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{3RT}{M}}$

Squaring and rearranging for $RT$ gives:
$RT = \dfrac{M v_{\text{rms}}^2}{3}$

For a rigid diatomic gas, the internal energy of one mole is:
$U = \dfrac{5}{2}RT$

Substituting the expression for $RT$ into the internal energy equation:
$U = \dfrac{5}{2} \left( \dfrac{M v_{\text{rms}}^2}{3} \right) = \dfrac{5}{6} M v_{\text{rms}}^2$

The molar mass must be converted to SI units:
$M = 30\text{ g mol}^{-1} = 0.03\text{ kg mol}^{-1}$

Now, substitute the given values:
$U = \dfrac{5}{6} \times 0.03 \times (600)^2$

$U = \dfrac{5}{6} \times 0.03 \times 360000$

$U = 5 \times 0.005 \times 360000 = 9000\text{ J}$.

Answer: $9000\text{ J}$

6a7a1ff816badb051d9daf96.text: A standard household alternating voltage supply has an RMS voltage of $220 \mathrm{~V}$ and a frequency of $50 \mathrm{~Hz}$. Which of the following equations correctly represents the instantaneous voltage $V(t)$?
6a7a1ff816badb051d9daf96.sol:
The peak voltage $V_0$ is related to the RMS voltage $V_{\mathrm{rms}}$ by the relation:
$V_0 = V_{\mathrm{rms}} \sqrt{2} = 220\sqrt{2} \mathrm{~V}$

The angular frequency $\omega$ is related to the linear frequency $f$ by the relation:
$\omega = 2\pi f = 2\pi \times 50 = 100\pi \mathrm{~rad/s}$

The standard equation for instantaneous alternating voltage is:
$V(t) = V_0 \sin(\omega t)$

Substituting the values, we get:
$V(t) = 220\sqrt{2} \sin(100\pi t)$

Answer: $V = 220\sqrt{2} \sin(100\pi t)$

6a7a1ff83cd4cfffa9b8c5f7.text: A prism of angle $A$ produces an angle of minimum deviation equal to $\dfrac{\pi}{2} - A$. The refractive index of the material of the prism is
6a7a1ff83cd4cfffa9b8c5f7.sol:
The refractive index $\mu$ of a prism is given by the formula:

$\mu = \dfrac{\sin\left(\dfrac{A + \delta_m}{2}\right)}{\sin\left(\dfrac{A}{2}\right)}$

Given that the angle of minimum deviation is $\delta_m = \dfrac{\pi}{2} - A$, we substitute this into the formula:

$\mu = \dfrac{\sin\left(\dfrac{A + \dfrac{\pi}{2} - A}{2}\right)}{\sin\left(\dfrac{A}{2}\right)}$

$\mu = \dfrac{\sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)}{\sin\left(\dfrac{A}{2}\right)}$

Since $\sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right) = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$, we get:

$\mu = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}\sin\left(\dfrac{A}{2}\right)}$

$\mu = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\csc\left(\dfrac{A}{2}\right)$

Answer: $\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\csc\left(\dfrac{A}{2}\right)$

6a7a1ff864fc1314c3511bcc.subject: Physics
6a7a1ff864fc1314c3511bcc.text: A point object is placed on the principal axis of a convex lens of focal length $15 \text{ cm}$ at a distance of $30 \text{ cm}$ from it. A convex mirror of radius of curvature $20 \text{ cm}$ is placed on the other side of the lens such that the principal axes of both the lens and the mirror coincide. If the final image formed by the combination coincides with the object itself, the distance between the convex lens and the convex mirror is ____ $\text{cm}$.
6a7a1ff864fc1314c3511bcc.sol:
For the final image to coincide with the object, the light rays must retrace their path after reflection from the convex mirror. This happens when the rays strike the mirror normally, meaning they are directed towards its centre of curvature.

First, find the position of the image formed by the convex lens alone.
Using the lens formula:
$\dfrac{1}{v} - \dfrac{1}{u} = \dfrac{1}{f}$

Given $u = -30 \text{ cm}$ and $f = +15 \text{ cm}$:
$\dfrac{1}{v} - \dfrac{1}{-30} = \dfrac{1}{15}$
$\dfrac{1}{v} = \dfrac{1}{15} - \dfrac{1}{30} = \dfrac{1}{30}$
$v = +30 \text{ cm}$

The image formed by the lens is at $30 \text{ cm}$ from the lens. For the rays to be directed towards the centre of curvature of the convex mirror, this image must be at a distance equal to the radius of curvature ($R = 20 \text{ cm}$) behind the mirror.

Let the distance between the lens and the mirror be $d$.
$d + R = v$
$d + 20 = 30$
$d = 10 \text{ cm}$

Answer: $10$

6a7a1ff8096d3d9ccae1d3d1.text: A Zener diode with a breakdown voltage of $10\ \text{V}$ is used to regulate the voltage across a variable load resistor $R_L$. The circuit is powered by a $30\ \text{V}$ DC supply through a series resistor of $400\ \Omega$. For the Zener diode to operate in the breakdown region and act as a voltage regulator, the minimum required value of the load resistance $R_L$ is
6a7a1ff8096d3d9ccae1d3d1.sol:
For the Zener diode to operate in the breakdown region, the voltage across the load terminals (with the Zener diode considered open-circuit) must be greater than or equal to the Zener breakdown voltage $V_Z$.

Using the voltage divider rule, the open-circuit voltage $V_{\text{oc}}$ across $R_L$ is:
$V_{\text{oc}} = V_{\text{in}} \times \dfrac{R_L}{R_s + R_L}$

Setting the condition $V_{\text{oc}} \ge V_Z$:
$30 \times \dfrac{R_L}{400 + R_L} \ge 10$

Dividing both sides by $10$:
$3 R_L \ge 400 + R_L$

$2 R_L \ge 400$

$R_L \ge 200\ \Omega$

Thus, the minimum required value of the load resistance is $200\ \Omega$.

Answer: $200\ \Omega$

6a7a1ff838220a68ee0526e2.text: The solubility product constant ($K_{\text{sp}}$) of $\text{Fe(OH)}_2$ at $298 \text{ K}$ is $4 \times 10^{-15}$. Let its solubility in pure water be $S_1$ and its solubility in a buffer solution of $\text{pH} = 11$ be $S_2$. The value of the ratio $\dfrac{S_1}{S_2}$ is ________.
6a7a1ff838220a68ee0526e2.sol:
First, calculate the solubility in pure water ($S_1$):
For $\text{Fe(OH)}_2$, the solubility product is given by:
$K_{\text{sp}} = 4S_1^3$
$4S_1^3 = 4 \times 10^{-15}$
$S_1^3 = 10^{-15}$
$S_1 = 10^{-5} \text{ mol/L}$

Next, calculate the solubility in the buffer solution ($S_2$):
Given $\text{pH} = 11$, the $\text{pOH}$ is $14 - 11 = 3$.
Therefore, the concentration of hydroxide ions is:
$[\text{OH}^-] = 10^{-3} \text{ M}$

In the buffer solution, the common ion effect dominates. The solubility $S_2$ is determined by:
$K_{\text{sp}} = [\text{Fe}^{2+}][\text{OH}^-]^2$
$4 \times 10^{-15} = S_2 (10^{-3})^2$
$4 \times 10^{-15} = S_2 \times 10^{-6}$
$S_2 = \dfrac{4 \times 10^{-15}}{10^{-6}} = 4 \times 10^{-9} \text{ mol/L}$

Finally, calculate the ratio $\dfrac{S_1}{S_2}$:
$\dfrac{S_1}{S_2} = \dfrac{10^{-5}}{4 \times 10^{-9}} = \dfrac{10^4}{4} = \dfrac{10000}{4} = 2500$

Answer: $2500$

6a7a1ff84fcbe6b6c5518d5b.text:
An element crystallises in a face-centred cubic (fcc) lattice with an edge length of $500 \text{ pm}$. If the density of the element is $4.0 \text{ g cm}^{-3}$, the molar mass of the element is _____ $\text{g mol}^{-1}$. (Nearest integer)

(Given: $N_A = 6.0 \times 10^{23} \text{ mol}^{-1}$)
6a7a1ff84fcbe6b6c5518d5b.sol:
For a face-centred cubic (fcc) lattice, the number of atoms per unit cell, $Z = 4$.

Edge length, $a = 500 \text{ pm} = 5 \times 10^{-8} \text{ cm}$

Density, $d = \dfrac{Z \times M}{N_A \times a^3}$

Rearranging for molar mass, $M = \dfrac{d \times N_A \times a^3}{Z}$

$M = \dfrac{4.0 \times 6.0 \times 10^{23} \times (5 \times 10^{-8})^3}{4}$

$M = 6.0 \times 10^{23} \times 125 \times 10^{-24}$

$M = 6.0 \times 12.5 = 75 \text{ g mol}^{-1}$

Answer: $75$

6a7a1ff885c50a846a305e08.subject: Chemistry
6a7a1ff885c50a846a305e08.text: The absolute difference in the squares of the spin-only magnetic moments of the complex ions $[Fe(H_2O)_6]^{2+}$ and $[Ru(H_2O)_6]^{2+}$ is ________ (in $\text{BM}^2$).
6a7a1ff885c50a846a305e08.sol:
For $[Fe(H_2O)_6]^{2+}$:
The central metal ion is $Fe^{2+}$, which has a $3d^6$ electronic configuration.
Since $H_2O$ acts as a weak field ligand for $3d$ series metals, the crystal field splitting is small ($\Delta_o < P$).
The electronic arrangement is $t_{2g}^4 e_g^2$, giving $4$ unpaired electrons ($n = 4$).
The square of the spin-only magnetic moment is $\mu_1^2 = n(n+2) = 4(4+2) = 24 \text{ BM}^2$.

For $[Ru(H_2O)_6]^{2+}$:
The central metal ion is $Ru^{2+}$, which belongs to the $4d$ series and has a $4d^6$ configuration.
For metals of the $4d$ and $5d$ series, the crystal field splitting is inherently large regardless of the ligand, so they always form low-spin complexes.
The electronic arrangement is $t_{2g}^6 e_g^0$, giving $0$ unpaired electrons ($n = 0$).
The square of the spin-only magnetic moment is $\mu_2^2 = 0(0+2) = 0 \text{ BM}^2$.

The absolute difference is $24 - 0 = 24$.

Answer: $24$

6a7a1ff80eaf91a5af3f954a.text:
Given below are two statements : one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A) : The boiling point of n-butyl alcohol is higher than that of tert-butyl alcohol, but both have higher boiling points than diethyl ether.

Reason (R) : Boiling points of alcohols decrease with an increase in branching due to a decrease in surface area, while alcohols have higher boiling points than isomeric ethers due to the presence of intermolecular hydrogen bonding.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
6a7a1ff80eaf91a5af3f954a.sol:
Assertion (A) is correct. n-butyl alcohol is a straight-chain alcohol and tert-butyl alcohol is its branched isomer. Both are alcohols and have higher boiling points than diethyl ether, which is an ether of comparable molecular mass.

Reason (R) is also correct and provides the exact physical explanation for the Assertion. For isomeric alcohols, as branching increases, the molecule becomes more spherical, which decreases the surface area and consequently weakens the van der Waals forces. This explains why n-butyl alcohol has a higher boiling point than tert-butyl alcohol. Furthermore, alcohols possess the ability to form intermolecular hydrogen bonds, requiring more energy to separate the molecules compared to the weak dipole-dipole interactions present in ethers like diethyl ether. This explains why both alcohols boil at higher temperatures than diethyl ether.

Thus, both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

Answer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)

6a7a1ff8f8426c64ff6dc7cc.text:
Consider the following sequence of reactions:

p-toluidine $\xrightarrow{\text{NaNO}_2, \text{ HCl, } 0-5^\circ\text{C}}$ (A) $\xrightarrow{\text{phenol, NaOH}}$ (B) $\xrightarrow{\text{(i) CHCl}_3\text{, NaOH, } \Delta \text{ (ii) H}_3\text{O}^+}$ (C)

The total number of $\text{sp}^2$ hybridized carbon atoms in the major product (C) is ________.
6a7a1ff8f8426c64ff6dc7cc.sol:
Step 1: p-toluidine (4-methylaniline) reacts with $\text{NaNO}_2$ and $\text{HCl}$ at $0-5^\circ\text{C}$ to form p-toluenediazonium chloride (A).

Step 2: The diazonium salt (A) couples with phenol in a basic medium. The coupling takes place at the para position of phenol, producing 4-(4-methylphenylazo)phenol (B).

Step 3: Compound (B) is subjected to the Reimer-Tiemann reaction conditions ($\text{CHCl}_3$ and $\text{NaOH}$, followed by acidic workup). The phenolic $-\text{OH}$ group strongly activates the ring towards electrophilic aromatic substitution. Since the para position is already occupied by the azo group, formylation occurs at the ortho position. The major product (C) is 2-hydroxy-5-(4-methylphenylazo)benzaldehyde.

The structure of (C) contains:
- One p-tolyl ring, which has 6 $\text{sp}^2$ hybridized carbons and 1 $\text{sp}^3$ hybridized carbon (the methyl group).
- One phenolic ring, which has 6 $\text{sp}^2$ hybridized carbons.
- One aldehyde group ($-\text{CHO}$), which has 1 $\text{sp}^2$ hybridized carbon.

Total number of $\text{sp}^2$ hybridized carbon atoms = $6 + 6 + 1 = 13$.

6a7a1ff8dba5b4a5a9ffd1de.text: Let $a_1, a_2, a_3, \dots$ be an arithmetic progression such that its third term is $10$ and its sixth term is $19$. Then the value of $4 \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \dfrac{a_n}{3^n}$ is equal to
6a7a1ff8dba5b4a5a9ffd1de.sol:
Let the first term be $a_1$ and the common difference be $d$.

Given $a_3 = a_1 + 2d = 10$ and $a_6 = a_1 + 5d = 19$.

Subtracting the two equations gives $3d = 9 \Rightarrow d = 3$.

Substituting $d = 3$ into the first equation gives $a_1 + 6 = 10 \Rightarrow a_1 = 4$.

Let $S = \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \dfrac{a_n}{3^n} = \dfrac{a_1}{3} + \dfrac{a_2}{3^2} + \dfrac{a_3}{3^3} + \dots$

This is an infinite arithmetico-geometric progression with common ratio $r = \dfrac{1}{3}$.

The sum of an infinite AGP is given by $S = \dfrac{a_1 r}{1-r} + \dfrac{d r^2}{(1-r)^2}$.

Substituting the values:

$S = \dfrac{4 \times \dfrac{1}{3}}{1 - \dfrac{1}{3}} + \dfrac{3 \times \left(\dfrac{1}{3}\right)^2}{\left(1 - \dfrac{1}{3}\right)^2}$

$S = \dfrac{4/3}{2/3} + \dfrac{3/9}{4/9} = 2 + \dfrac{3}{4} = \dfrac{11}{4}$

Therefore, $4S = 4 \times \dfrac{11}{4} = 11$.

Answer: $11$

6a7a1ff8306a671f534d3e2b.text: Let circle $C_1$ be given by the equation $x^2 + y^2 - 10x - 16y + 85 = 0$. It is reflected across a line $L$ to form circle $C_2$. Let $A$ be the rightmost point on $C_2$. If point $B(0, \sqrt{3})$ lies on $C_2$ such that the length of the minor arc $AB$ is $(1/6)^{\text{th}}$ of the perimeter of $C_2$, and the $y$-coordinate of $B$ is strictly greater than the $y$-coordinate of $A$, then if the equation of the line $L$ is written in the form $3x + 4y = c$, the value of $c$ is
6a7a1ff8306a671f534d3e2b.sol:
The equation of circle $C_1$ can be written as $(x-5)^2 + (y-8)^2 = 4$.
Thus, the centre of $C_1$ is $(5, 8)$ and its radius is $r = 2$.
Since $C_2$ is the reflection of $C_1$, it also has a radius of $r = 2$. Let its centre be $(h, k)$.
Point $A$ is the rightmost point on $C_2$, so its parametric angle is $0$. Thus, $A = (h+2, k)$.
The length of the minor arc $AB$ is $(1/6)^{\text{th}}$ of the perimeter of $C_2$, which means the angle subtended by arc $AB$ at the centre is $\dfrac{1}{6} \times 2\pi = \dfrac{\pi}{3}$.
Since the $y$-coordinate of $B$ is greater than that of $A$, the parametric angle for $B$ is $+\dfrac{\pi}{3}$.
The coordinates of $B$ are $(h + 2\cos(\pi/3), k + 2\sin(\pi/3)) = (h + 1, k + \sqrt{3})$.
We are given that $B$ is $(0, \sqrt{3})$, so:
$h + 1 = 0 \Rightarrow h = -1$
$k + \sqrt{3} = \sqrt{3} \Rightarrow k = 0$
The centre of $C_2$ is $(-1, 0)$.
The line of reflection $L$ is the perpendicular bisector of the line segment joining the centres $(5, 8)$ and $(-1, 0)$.
The midpoint of this segment is $\left(\dfrac{5-1}{2}, \dfrac{8+0}{2}\right) = (2, 4)$.
The slope of the segment joining the centres is $\dfrac{8-0}{5-(-1)} = \dfrac{8}{6} = \dfrac{4}{3}$.
Therefore, the slope of line $L$ is $-\dfrac{3}{4}$.
The equation of line $L$ is $y - 4 = -\dfrac{3}{4}(x - 2)$.
$\Rightarrow 4y - 16 = -3x + 6$
$\Rightarrow 3x + 4y = 22$
Comparing this with $3x + 4y = c$, we get $c = 22$.

Answer: $22$

6a7a1ff8d307ba07c562d819.text: Let $PQ$ be a focal chord of the parabola $y^2 = 16x$ of length $25$, and let $V$ be the vertex of the parabola. If $G(\alpha, \beta)$ is the centroid of the triangle $PVQ$ with $\beta > 0$, then the value of $3\alpha + \beta^2$ is
6a7a1ff8d307ba07c562d819.sol:
For the parabola $y^2 = 16x$, we have $a = 4$. The vertex is $V(0, 0)$.

Let the endpoints of the focal chord be $P(4t^2, 8t)$ and $Q\left(\dfrac{4}{t^2}, -\dfrac{8}{t}\right)$.
The length of a focal chord is given by $a\left(t + \dfrac{1}{t}\right)^2$.
Given that the length is $25$:
$4\left(t + \dfrac{1}{t}\right)^2 = 25$
$\Rightarrow \left(t + \dfrac{1}{t}\right)^2 = \dfrac{25}{4}$

We can find $t^2 + \dfrac{1}{t^2}$ as follows:
$t^2 + \dfrac{1}{t^2} = \left(t + \dfrac{1}{t}\right)^2 - 2 = \dfrac{25}{4} - 2 = \dfrac{17}{4}$

We also need $t - \dfrac{1}{t}$ to find the $y$-coordinate of the centroid:
$\left(t - \dfrac{1}{t}\right)^2 = \left(t + \dfrac{1}{t}\right)^2 - 4 = \dfrac{25}{4} - 4 = \dfrac{9}{4}$
$\Rightarrow t - \dfrac{1}{t} = \pm \dfrac{3}{2}$

The centroid $G(\alpha, \beta)$ of $\triangle PVQ$ is:
$\alpha = \dfrac{4t^2 + \dfrac{4}{t^2} + 0}{3} = \dfrac{4}{3}\left(t^2 + \dfrac{1}{t^2}\right) = \dfrac{4}{3} \times \dfrac{17}{4} = \dfrac{17}{3}$

$\beta = \dfrac{8t - \dfrac{8}{t} + 0}{3} = \dfrac{8}{3}\left(t - \dfrac{1}{t}\right)$
Since it is given that $\beta > 0$, we must choose $t - \dfrac{1}{t} = \dfrac{3}{2}$.
$\beta = \dfrac{8}{3} \times \dfrac{3}{2} = 4$

We need to find the value of $3\alpha + \beta^2$:
$3\left(\dfrac{17}{3}\right) + (4)^2 = 17 + 16 = 33$.

Answer: $33$

6a7a1ff8614fa44a82f77793.text: The mean and variance of $7$ observations are $11$ and $36$ respectively. If five of these observations are $2, 5, 14, 17$ and $20$, and the remaining two are $a$ and $b$ ($a \gt b$), then the mean deviation about the median of all the $7$ observations is
6a7a1ff8614fa44a82f77793.sol:
Let the remaining two observations be $a$ and $b$.
Given, Mean $= 11$
$\Rightarrow \dfrac{2 + 5 + 14 + 17 + 20 + a + b}{7} = 11$
$\Rightarrow 58 + a + b = 77 \Rightarrow a + b = 19$

Given, Variance $= 36$
$\Rightarrow \dfrac{2^2 + 5^2 + 14^2 + 17^2 + 20^2 + a^2 + b^2}{7} - 11^2 = 36$
$\Rightarrow \dfrac{4 + 25 + 196 + 289 + 400 + a^2 + b^2}{7} - 121 = 36$
$\Rightarrow 914 + a^2 + b^2 = 7 \times 157 = 1099$
$\Rightarrow a^2 + b^2 = 185$

We have $(a + b)^2 = a^2 + b^2 + 2ab$
$\Rightarrow 361 = 185 + 2ab \Rightarrow 2ab = 176 \Rightarrow ab = 88$
The values of $a$ and $b$ are the roots of $t^2 - 19t + 88 = 0$
$\Rightarrow (t - 11)(t - 8) = 0$
Since $a \gt b$, we get $a = 11$ and $b = 8$.

The $7$ observations in ascending order are: $2, 5, 8, 11, 14, 17, 20$.
Median $= 4^{\text{th}}$ observation $= 11$.

Mean deviation about the median $= \dfrac{\sum |x_i - \text{Median}|}{7}$
$= \dfrac{|2 - 11| + |5 - 11| + |8 - 11| + |11 - 11| + |14 - 11| + |17 - 11| + |20 - 11|}{7}$
$= \dfrac{9 + 6 + 3 + 0 + 3 + 6 + 9}{7} = \dfrac{36}{7}$.

Answer: $\dfrac{36}{7}$

6a7a1ff86c958228c4df7a41.text: Let $I_n = \int_0^{\pi/2} \dfrac{\sin 2nx}{\cos x} dx$ for $n \in \mathbb{N}$. Then the value of $\sum_{k=1}^{15} \dfrac{2}{I_{k+1} + I_k}$ is equal to
6a7a1ff86c958228c4df7a41.sol:
Given $I_n = \int_0^{\pi/2} \dfrac{\sin 2nx}{\cos x} dx$

Consider $I_{k+1} + I_k = \int_0^{\pi/2} \dfrac{\sin(2k+2)x + \sin 2kx}{\cos x} dx$

Using the identity $\sin C + \sin D = 2 \sin\left(\dfrac{C+D}{2}\right) \cos\left(\dfrac{C-D}{2}\right)$, we get:

$I_{k+1} + I_k = \int_0^{\pi/2} \dfrac{2\sin(2k+1)x \cos x}{\cos x} dx$

$= 2 \int_0^{\pi/2} \sin(2k+1)x dx$

$= 2 \left[ \dfrac{-\cos(2k+1)x}{2k+1} \right]_0^{\pi/2}$

$= 2 \left( 0 - \left( \dfrac{-1}{2k+1} \right) \right) = \dfrac{2}{2k+1}$

Therefore, $\dfrac{2}{I_{k+1} + I_k} = 2k+1$

Now, we need to evaluate the sum:

$\sum_{k=1}^{15} (2k+1) = 3 + 5 + 7 + \dots + 31$

This is an arithmetic progression with $15$ terms, first term $a = 3$, and last term $l = 31$.

Sum $= \dfrac{15}{2} (3 + 31) = \dfrac{15}{2} (34) = 15 \times 17 = 255$.

Answer: $255$
